props.title: Why India Needs More Playgrounds: A Look at the Current State of Play Spaces
props.summaryText: Open space is shrinking in Indian cities and many villages have no play equipment at all. Who loses out, why it matters, and what different groups can do to change it.
props.author: meera-iyer
props.imageAlt: Students seated in a school classroom in India

takeaways.text: Open play space in Indian cities is shrinking as land goes to buildings, roads and parking.
Many villages and government schools have open land but little safe play equipment.
Girls, children with disabilities and children in low-income areas are most affected.
Cities, schools, builders, companies and communities can each add or restore play spaces.

faq.q: Why does India need more playgrounds?
faq.a: Because open spaces in cities are disappearing, many schools and villages lack safe play equipment, and play is essential for children's health, development and wellbeing. Children without safe places to play often play on streets or not at all.

faq.q: Who is most affected by the lack of playgrounds in India?
faq.a: Children in low-income urban areas, girls whose movement is restricted to nearby spaces, children with disabilities who cannot use typical equipment, and children in villages and government schools without equipment.

faq.q: How can more playgrounds be created in India?
faq.a: Through city planning that protects open space, play areas in every housing project, better school playgrounds, CSR funding for under-served areas, inclusive design, and maintenance of existing parks.
